Analysis masks define the cells included in each Study Area, Stream and Reach for
a Survey Event. They supply the common grid and spatial domain used by DEM
processing. Saving or opening an Event prepares or reuses its masks automatically.

## Grid and raster values

The saved Study analysis CRS and Event cell size define the grid. Study Area
bounds are snapped outward to the shared anchor. Stream and Reach masks occupy
aligned subwindows and intersect their parent masks. A value of 1 denotes the
analysis domain; cells outside it, including polygon holes, are NoData.

`fluvgeo::write_event_masks()` uses terra `rasterize(touches=FALSE)`, `classify`,
`crop` and `mask`. Outputs are compressed, file-backed Byte GeoTIFFs with BigTIFF
support. A mask defines spatial membership; source DEM NoData remains NoData
when the mask is applied.

Grid coordinates belong to the saved real-world CRS. The implementation uses a
shared numeric anchor; confirmation of its initial-placement convention remains
an open design decision in `dev/features/dem-mosaic-design.md`. Saved grids are
preserved until that decision is resolved.

## Preparation and reuse

`event_masks_server()` queues assigned Streams and obtains requests through
`store$mask_request()`. It searches published editions with `find_masks()` and
runs a background worker to verify a reusable edition or write the required masks.
`fluvgeo::event_mask_key()` identifies geometry, grid and processing dependencies.
Records without a dependency key use exact input matching.

Streams share the Study Area mask through a filesystem hard link when available,
with copying as a fallback. Reopening uses metadata checks; explicit backend
checksum verification is available for integrity investigations. Large outputs
use terra's file-backed processing. Resource failures are reported by the worker.

## Publication and session lifecycle

A completed mask edition is published only while its saved input revisions still
match. Input changes, cancellation and session closure stop workers before owned
staging is cleaned. Published editions remain available. Staging-owner records
permit recovery after both the app and worker have exited; unknown ownership
prevents automatic cleanup.

The DEM queue waits for mask readiness. Routine mask preparation has no analyst
controls or progress display; actionable failures identify the relevant settings.
An optional diagnostic view is documented separately in
[terrain developer tools](terrain-developer-tools.html).

## Implementation and tests

Trace `R/event_masks.R`, `R/study_store.R` and `R/survey_event_settings.R`.
`test-event-masks.R` covers orchestration, reuse, stale inputs and cleanup. The
scientific contract and raster tests belong to fluvgeo:
`dev/schemas/event-masks.md` and `test_event_masks.R`.

## Data objects and storage

See [Data objects and local storage](storage-model.html) for the FGDB ownership and physical representation crosswalk.

| Operation | Data object read or changed | Physical representation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write_event_masks()` | Reads Study/Stream/Reach polygons and Event grid settings | GeoPackage hierarchy geometry, reference and settings tables |
| Mask publication / `read_event_masks()` | Creates/reads processing-domain rasters and their input associations | External Byte GeoTIFFs and mask manifest |
| `mask_terrain_mosaic()` | Uses the domain to constrain terrain cells | Reads mask and elevation GeoTIFFs; produces masked elevation GeoTIFF |

Masks represent analysis membership, not a governed FGDB terrain observation or
feature class. Their parent IDs and grid association relate them to domain objects.
